subject: Computer Networking
title: Egypt's Anchor Drag (2013)
description: A quick win: understand Egypt's Anchor Drag (2013).

hook.text: In 2013, Egyptian authorities arrested divers cutting a cable. But most cable damage comes from anchors.

buildup.text: Ships dragging anchors in shallow water near cable landing points are the top cause of undersea cable damage.

discovery.text: Mediterranean and Red Sea cables carry traffic between Europe, the Middle East, and Asia. Heavily concentrated.

twist.text: In 2008, multiple cuts near Egypt knocked out 70% of India's internet. Millions of users were affected.

climax.text: Cable protection zones restrict anchoring. But enforcement is hard, and fishing boats often ignore them.

punchline.text: A dragged anchor can disconnect entire countries.

quiz.question: What is the leading cause of undersea cable damage?
options: Ships dragging anchors in shallow water near cables
Shark bites on deep-sea cable segments

details.summary: In 2013, Egyptian authorities arrested divers who were attempting to cut an undersea fiber optic cable near Alexandria. The cable carried a significant portion of internet traffic between Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.
details.whyItMatters: Most international internet traffic flows through undersea cables that are physically vulnerable. Cable cuts create bottlenecks that affect entire regions.
takeaways: Undersea cables carry over 95% of international data
Physical damage to cables affects entire regions of connectivity
Cable routes are concentrated through geographical chokepoints

faq.question: How vulnerable are undersea internet cables?
faq.answer: Extremely. Cables are typically only the diameter of a garden hose and lie on the ocean floor. Ship anchors, fishing trawls, and earthquakes cause over 100 cable faults annually. Most redundancy comes from having multiple cables on different routes.

faq.question: What happens when a major undersea cable is cut?
faq.answer: Traffic automatically reroutes through alternative cables, but the remaining cables may become congested. If multiple cables on the same route are cut, entire countries can lose connectivity. Repair ships take days or weeks to reach the break and splice the fiber.
